text: The Keasling group's high-titer artemisinic acid production pathway (mevalonate pathway to amorphadiene to artemisinic acid) was engineered to completion, including the CYP71AV1 oxidation steps, primarily in which host organism?
explanation: The complete high-titer pathway, reaching about 25 g/L artemisinic acid, was engineered into Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's yeast), which has an endogenous mevalonate pathway well suited to terpenoid production; E. coli was used only for partial-pathway proof-of-concept work. Bacillus subtilis and Pichia pastoris were not the hosts used in this landmark case study.
